proposal.title: Chunk published fields by individual full-field samples
proposal.hypothesis: Operational evidence shows the measured consumer workload is warm-cache, shuffled full-field tensor access over 28 samples with sample shape [3, 721, 1440], while provider/cache changes cannot improve it. If each published data variable is written with chunks aligned to one time sample, the consumer should read each shuffled full-field sample using one spatially contiguous chunk per channel instead of assembling it from several spatial chunks, increasing consumer_samples_per_second without changing names, selectors, coordinates, metadata validation, or public interface.
proposal.expected_tradeoffs: This may change chunk object count and compression efficiency slightly, so output_bytes and materialization_seconds could move modestly in either direction. The intended causal effect is faster warm shuffled full-field reads through access-pattern-aligned chunking.

edits.old_text: encoding = {name: {} for name in list(ds.data_vars) + list(ds.coords)}
edits.rationale: Aligns data chunks with the evaluator's shuffled full-field sample access pattern by storing one complete latitude-longitude field per time/channel chunk, while leaving coordinate publication and validation intact.

proposal.validation_plan: Rerun the evaluator and compare consumer_samples_per_second against the baseline 44.985 samples/s. Confirm contract correctness, semantic equivalence, rerun safety, provenance/security, consolidated Zarr v3 output, frozen array paths, selector coordinate paths, and validation still pass.
